questions.stem: Two events are mutually exclusive. This means:

options.text: They cannot happen at the same time

questions.explanation: Mutually exclusive events cannot occur at the same time. If one happens, the other cannot. For example, when rolling a die, getting a $3$ and getting a $5$ are mutually exclusive.

questions.stem: A fair die is rolled. $P(\text{even}) = \frac{3}{6}$ and $P(5) = \frac{1}{6}$. What is $P(\text{even or } 5)$?
questions.explanation: Getting an even number and getting $5$ are mutually exclusive (they cannot both happen on one roll). So $P(\text{even or } 5) = P(\text{even}) + P(5) = \frac{3}{6} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$.
